items.name: Iranian mine claims 23-24 Nov vs confirmation: 1 new claim-event - IRGC Navy (IRNA, Mon 23 Nov, 'in the last few hours'): 'three violating oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz' suffered 'severe explosions and fires after striking naval mines' on 'unauthorised' routes, one off the southern shores and two in the east of the strait, 'while under extensive air escort by the US army' which 'failed to prevent the incidents'; images promised; US cover 'will not serve as a substitute' for compliance with the IRGC Navy Traffic Control Center. Iran International 24 Nov 08:47Z carries a navy version: 'two tankers hit mines east of Strait of Hormuz' ('a tanker exploded and caught fire'). Confirmed by any maritime authority: 0 (JMIC: mine claims 'unverified'; CENTCOM no response)
items.source: JPost 24 Nov 00:23 (IRNA statement text); Euronews 24 Nov 10:42Z; Arab News/Reuters 24 Nov (Press TV relay); Gulf News 24 Nov 11:05 GST; nation.com.pk 24 Nov 09:31Z (Azmayi); Iran International liveblog 24 Nov 08:47Z
items.note: Counted as one claim-event (three hulls); the 'two tankers' Iran International entry may be the same statement or the 22 Nov 'two more supertankers' claim re-relayed - unresolved. New element: the claim is framed as defeating a US air escort, i.e. Iran now asserts mines against escorted traffic, not only dark ships. IRGC Navy chief Ali Azmayi (Iranian media, 24 Nov): ships must follow designated routes; the strait 'was not a place to test unauthorized routes' (paraphrase). Cumulative IRGC/Artesh mine claims since 21 Nov: 1 (Al Ghanam) + 2 supertankers (22 Nov) + 3 (23 Nov) = 6 hulls claimed, 0 confirmed.

items.name: OFAC Iran actions in gate: 1 - Mon 23 Nov 'Iran-related Designations' (Operation Economic Outcast, 'Iran's global shadow banking networks'): 8 individuals + 22 entities added to the SDN list (IRAN-EO13902: 7 individuals / 21 entities; IRAN-EO13871: Robust Trading LLC; SDGT + IFSR: H N B Trading Co LLC); no vessels. Named (gCaptain): Dubai-based OGA Global General Trading, H N B Trading, Gespl International, Integral Petro Energy Trading; Iran Center for Exchange of Currency and Gold; Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars (military-linked); Dragon Road Ltd; Kharg Petrochemical Co; NITC payment networks and NIOC as beneficiary; tanker SERENE I (IMO 9197832) cited in a chartering arrangement (not stated as designated). Treasury: 'no Iranian oil had been loaded onto vessels since Operation Economic Outcast began on August 24'. Bessent (late Mon): 'Iran's economy is under water, and its leaders are panicking'
items.source: ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261123 (primary; counts and programs); gCaptain 23 Nov 12:36 PST (names); The National 24 Nov (Bessent quote); Iran International liveblog 24 Nov 09:04Z (dollar through 2.8 million rials on the open market Tuesday); Treasury press release sb0699 client_error
items.note: T-panel sanctions tell: a 30-target financial-plumbing action on the day Doha's PM sat with Rubio and Vance - the sanctions track is tightening while the mediator track is publicly 'appreciated' but unproductive. The 'no oil loaded since 24 Aug' claim is Treasury's and sits against the IRGC/Hamshahri convoy narrative and UANI's 'no significant loading at Kharg'. WSJ (Mon, via IBT/Yahoo 24 Nov 11:40Z): US investigating whether Iran was behind cyberattacks on as many as 50 commercial vessels (oil, LPG, chemicals; some with bomb threats; VL Prosperity and Kohaku boarded in Aug; Russia also examined); a Trump administration official: the US 'had not found evidence indicating Iranian involvement'.

items.name: Qatari PM/FM Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani in Washington Mon 23 Nov: met Rubio at State (8th US-Qatar Strategic Dialogue; readout: Rubio 'expressed appreciation for Qatar's global mediation efforts' and stressed 'continued close coordination' to deter threats; joint statement 'shared policy priorities', no new policy) and Vance at the White House (~10 minutes per AP's source; Vance's office no comment); Al Thani after the Rubio talks: the region 'cannot bear a renewed escalation of tensions between the United States and Iran', Doha 'working to bring both sides back to the table', Qatar and the US seeking stronger military cooperation; AP: mediators have proposed lifting Hormuz disruptions in exchange for LIMITED Iranian sanctions relief, opening broader talks including the nuclear programme; AP: Trump told Vance the administration 'did not need a deal with Iran' and to focus on fraud/crime in Democratic-led cities. Tehran follow-through on the summons: Iran calls Qatar's position in the German-Qatari statement 'unexpected' (Gulf News 24 Nov 04:53 GST); chief negotiator via Fars: 'There will be no actions or negotiations until Iran's seven conditions are met'; Ghalibaf: position unchanged, US threats 'a sign of the Americans' desperation', demands 'conveyed to Washington' and awaiting a response; Gharibabadi (23 Nov 04:23Z, pre-gate): 'the window of diplomacy is still open'

items.note: T3: the Washington leg of the Qatari shuttle produced a courtesy readout, a 10-minute VP meeting and no Trump engagement, on the day Tehran publicly discounted Doha; the AP 'Hormuz-for-limited-relief' proposal is the first printed shape of a bridging deal (sequencing: strait first, sanctions second, nuclear later) and is the item to watch for an Iranian response - Tehran's same-day line is 'no negotiations until seven conditions are met'. Trump-told-Vance 'did not need a deal' (AP, sourced) is a T1 negative. No Omani, Turkish or Witkoff contact surfaced; no new Trump Iran statement Mon-Tue beyond the Monday Truth Social (recorded 11-23); AP: 'no Trump statement specifically on Monday'.

items.name: Iran formalises Hormuz as the lever, Mon 23 - Tue 24 Nov: Army C-in-C Maj Gen Amir Hatami, at a senior command meeting citing orders from Mojtaba Khamenei, orders Navy chief Shahram Irani: 'Until the seven conditions set by the Islamic Republic of Iran are fulfilled, the Strait of Hormuz will not only remain closed' but 'its closure must become increasingly stringent day by day'; the strait 'represents geopolitical power'; a new US war would bring blows 'more severe, more crushing and without geographical limitation' (IRIB; TASS/Euronews date the order Mon 23 vs Tue 24 Nov); Ghalibaf: 'There are military ways to break the blockade, and we will pursue them in the near future'; earlier (23 Nov 04:14 GST): Iran cannot remain in 'neither war nor peace', 'we must remove the threat from our country', calls for 'sustainable deterrence'; Baghaei: the blockade is 'tantamount to military aggression', Iran will use all available means; Mokhber (Khamenei adviser) on X: 'Take a lesson from the Strait of Hormuz'; Fars: if 'one bullet' hits an Iranian tanker, Gulf Arab oil terminals could be targeted; seven conditions as relayed (TASS lists five): lift sanctions, unfreeze assets, end the blockade, war-damage compensation, halt regional hostilities incl. Lebanon

items.note: T1 (Iranian side): the first formal military ORDER tying the strait's closure to the seven conditions and escalating it 'day by day' - previously the linkage was ministerial rhetoric (Araghchi 21 Nov 'pointless'). Paired with the IRGC 'mined under US escort' claim, the Azmayi routing warning and the Fars terminal threat, the Iranian posture hardened on the same day the market sold the risk premium by 3.5%. Dating caveat: TASS says the order came 'on Tuesday', Euronews 'on Monday'; recorded as_of 24 Nov (publication).

items.name: Strike-planning read (Iran International, 23 Nov 04:23Z, lead only; Axios/WSJ/Bloomberg sourcing): Trump 'considering postponing renewed strikes on Iran' despite Israeli pressure - Mossad chief Roman Gofman travelled to Washington the week before to urge resumed joint strikes (Axios, WSJ); Bloomberg, citing British government assessments: Britain and several Arab Gulf states privately urged Washington not to launch new strikes, fearing Iranian retaliation and prolonged energy disruption; Trump: Saudi Arabia asked him 'to please just let it be the way it is now for a while'; Trump (Fox 22 Nov): negotiators are 'professional tap dancers', indirect talks continuing; Gharibabadi: 'the window of diplomacy is still open', Iran 'ready for any scenario'

items.name: Maritime regime, 23-24 Nov: IRGC Navy claims three 'violating' tankers mined and ablaze Mon 23 Nov 'while under extensive air escort by the US army' (one south, two east of the strait; images promised; CENTCOM no response; JMIC 'unverified'); IRGC Navy chief Azmayi warns ships off 'unauthorized routes'; Iran navy claims a US LUCAS drone downed east of the strait (uncorroborated); UKMTO: no new advisory dated 23-24 Nov surfaced; the 22 Nov Gulf of Oman 'military forces' incident is Advisory 217-26 (~1425Z) and a maritime-security analyst's X post says the US struck a tanker exporting Iranian oil under the blockade (no US/Iranian confirmation); JMIC names Torkel (215-26) and Arina (216-26), logs 114 US-assisted passages 19-21 Nov, threat SEVERE; Gulf News: ~28 US-facilitated transits/day, 227 vessels stationary east of the strait; hormuz.now AIS crossings 3 (Sun) / 4 (Mon), 7-day 7.7/day; straits.live 54 holding; Kharg convoy walked back: IRIB (Mon): 'a convoy of Iranian tankers has not set sail to break the US naval blockade' though Iran has 'various methods to bypass and break the blockade'; Foreign Ministry: loading reports are 'speculation'; unverified reports the SNSC halted the 14 tankers; Iran International 24 Nov 10:03Z: 'Iranian media walk back tanker convoy claims after days of blockade-breaking hype'
items.headline: Maritime regime, 23-24 Nov: IRGC Navy claims three 'violating' tankers mined and ablaze Mon 23 Nov 'while under extensive air escort by the US army' (one south, two east of the strait; images promised; CENTCOM no response; JMIC 'unverified'); IRGC Navy chief Azmayi warns ships off 'unauthorized routes'; Iran navy claims a US LUCAS drone downed east of the strait (uncorroborated); UKMTO: no new advisory dated 23-24 Nov surfaced; the 22 Nov Gulf of Oman 'military forces' incident is Advisory 217-26 (~1425Z) and a maritime-security analyst's X post says the US struck a tanker exporting Iranian oil under the blockade (no US/Iranian confirmation); JMIC names Torkel (215-26) and Arina (216-26), logs 114 US-assisted passages 19-21 Nov, threat SEVERE; Gulf News: ~28 US-facilitated transits/day, 227 vessels stationary east of the strait; hormuz.now AIS crossings 3 (Sun) / 4 (Mon), 7-day 7.7/day; straits.live 54 holding; Kharg convoy walked back: IRIB (Mon): 'a convoy of Iranian tankers has not set sail to break the US naval blockade' though Iran has 'various methods to bypass and break the blockade'; Foreign Ministry: loading reports are 'speculation'; unverified reports the SNSC halted the 14 tankers; Iran International 24 Nov 10:03Z: 'Iranian media walk back tanker convoy claims after days of blockade-breaking hype'
items.source: JPost 24 Nov 00:23; Euronews 24 Nov 10:42Z; balitangmarino 24 Nov 04:17Z; Gulf News 24 Nov 11:05 GST and live 23 Nov 05:53 GST; The National 24 Nov 10:05 (IRIB denial, SNSC reports); Iran International liveblog 24 Nov 08:47Z / 10:03Z; straits.live 23 Nov brief; hormuz.now/traffic 23 Nov 22:58Z; nation.com.pk 24 Nov
items.note: M-panel: the convoy test did NOT happen (state broadcaster denial = the Iranian side stepping back from the blockade-breaking test Trump dared on 22 Nov), while the Iranian claim set shifts from 'dark ships hit mines' to 'US-escorted tankers hit mines' - a claim of denying the US-facilitated lane itself, unconfirmed by UKMTO/JMIC. The open fact from 11-23 (nature of 217-26) is narrowed to 'possible US interdiction of an Iranian-oil tanker per one analyst' - still unconfirmed; a confirmation would be a HARD-EVENT (convoy/blockade interdiction). AIS flow stayed collapsed (3, 4/day) while the US-facilitated lane (JMIC 114 passages over 3 days) carried most traffic - the two counters now describe two different regimes.

items.name: Oil structure, Mon 23 Nov settle and Tue 24 Nov Asia: Brent Jan settled 89.37 (-3.20, -3.46%, lowest close since 28 Aug), WTI Jan 80.17 (-3.24, -3.88%, lowest since 7 Aug) - the largest daily move of the November sequence, down, through a day of Iranian escalation (Hatami order, three-tanker mine claim) and new OFAC sanctions; drivers printed: Libya Sharara pipeline reopened (~350 kb/d), Deutsche Bank 'rebalancing and turning into surplus' (1.7 mb/d; observed inventories +52 mb in Oct), JPMorgan 'production will exceed demand', Reuters poll +0.9 mb US stocks, Goldman oversupply warning, IEA surplus this quarter and larger in 2027; equities +4.73% S&P / +6.51% Nasdaq (Nvidia +31%); Tuesday Asia: Brent 88.71 at 03:10Z (-0.7%) -> 88.97 -> 88.28 (untimed) -> 89.62 (+0.28%, tradingeconomics later), WTI 79.57 / 79.18; DBS: 'lost any upward impetus... supply conditions remain benign' but 'risk of prices going up again cannot be ruled out as nothing has moved in US-Iran talks'; ANZ: 'from acute scarcity towards persistent vulnerability'; tradingeconomics: 'Brent declines on US-Iran optimism' (Qatari shuttle); Feb settle / Jan-Feb spread unprinted (last 2.48 intraday Mon 06:32Z); Brent-WTI Jan 9.20 at settle; Brent -22.4% over four weeks (TE); OPEC+ ministerial Sun 29 Nov (2027 quotas); Jan Brent expiry Mon 30 Nov; US oil rigs +6 to 469; WSJ: US probing Iran's role in cyberattacks on up to 50 ships

The market is pricing physical supply (Libya back, surplus research) and the US-facilitated lane (JMIC 114 passages/3 days), not AIS crossings (7.7/day). Prompt structure unobservable this run (no Feb print). Watch: OPEC+ Sun 29 Nov, Jan expiry 30 Nov, and whether the 217-26 incident resolves to a US interdiction. Brent's daily move (-3.20) is below the USD 5 HARD-EVENT threshold.
